narrative.h2: Lyric videos earn their place when the typography is the show

sections.heading: What a real lyric video is
sections.body: Lyric video used to be the cheap option labels released first while the 'real' MV finished post. That's no longer true - Bob Dylan's Subterranean Homesick Blues (1965) was the original kinetic-text video, and modern lyric videos from Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, and the Genius vertical have become primary releases. The format's discipline is type: kerning, weight, transition timing on every word, type-as-image where the word becomes the visual. Anything less is a karaoke screen.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: Lyric video is the right format when the lyrics carry the song (storytelling singer-songwriter, rap with dense wordplay, pop hooks built on phrasing), when the artist isn't filming themselves (debut releases, anonymous projects), when the goal is sing-along virality on TikTok, or as a Day 1 release while a narrative MV finishes. Canon examples: D.A. Pennebaker's Bob Dylan Subterranean Homesick Blues card-drop (1965), Bruce Gowers' Queen Bohemian Rhapsody lyric overlay tradition, Meghan Trainor's All About That Bass directed by Fatima Robinson, Ariana Grande's BBNG-animated Confessions, Ian Sherman's word-by-word animator work. Genius's vertical lyric content has trained an entire generation to expect word-by-word visual emphasis. Hip-hop especially benefits - the visual makes dense bars legible on first listen.

sections.heading: Tunee prompting tip
sections.body: Pick a single typographic system per video: one typeface, two weights, one accent color. 'Helvetica Neue Bold, white on black, single magenta accent for hook words'. Specify motion language: 'words appear word-by-word on syllable, fade out on next phrase' versus 'whole lines slide in left-to-right'. Reference a director if you have one: 'Kyle Cooper title-sequence energy' or 'David Carson collage layout'. Avoid generic 'animated text' - type direction is the whole craft here.
